Fat %1$s g × 0.45 + Protein %2$s g × 0.20 = +%3$s g (estimated delayed carbs)
Note: Apply enters only the %1$d g immediate carbs. To dose the %2$d g FPU delayed portion as eCarbs over ~%3$d h, add a second entry manually via the Carbs menu.
FPU: fat %1$s g + protein %2$s g → +%3$s g delayed

These only store the profile. To use it, do a profile switch (also after overwriting the active profile).
Run Autotune for the last 7 days with the current profile? This replaces the last Autotune result.
%1$s was overwritten with the last suggestion. If you run a new review, \'Revert\' will no longer restore the values from before that overwrite. Continue?
Running Autotune… this can take a minute.
Autotune could not calculate a result. Usually there is too little data (BG readings, carbs) in the last 7 days.
No review yet. Tap \'Run review\' to analyse the last 7 days.
Store the suggestion as a new local profile?\n%1$s\nThe profile in use is not changed.
Saved as %1$s. Use a profile switch to activate it.
Replace basal, ISF and IC of %1$s with the suggested values?\nYou can undo it with \'Revert\'.
Restore %1$s to the values from before the overwrite?
BG rose without meals at %1$s on %3$d of %2$d days (deviation sum %4$s) → the basal before it was raised.
BG fell without meals at %1$s on %3$d of %2$d days (deviation sum %4$s) → the basal before it was lowered.
At %1$s the rises and falls cancel out (deviation sum %2$s), so it stays.
No basal-only data at %1$s, so it stays.
Meals overlapped, so there was no basal-only period → it only followed the neighbouring hours a little.
It stopped at the upper limit (%1$d%% of the current basal).
It stopped at the lower limit (%1$d%% of the current basal).
Basal is fixed 1–3 hours before the hour where BG moved (basal acts late). Each day only 20%% of the needed change is applied, adding up over %1$d days.
Daily average %1$s ÷ ISF %2$s = %3$s U short → 20%% of it spread over the 3 hours before, every day
Daily average %1$s ÷ ISF %2$s = %3$s U too much → 20%% of it taken off the 3 hours before, every day
%1$d correction periods without meals: BG dropped only about %2$d%% of what was expected, so 1 U is now assumed to lower BG less.
%1$d correction periods without meals: BG dropped about %2$d%% of what was expected, so 1 U is now assumed to lower BG more.
%1$d correction periods: BG dropped about %2$d%% of what was expected, close enough to keep ISF.
%1$d correction periods (median %2$d%% of the expected drop), tuned day by day.
Days with fewer than 10 correction periods keep ISF unchanged (this week: %1$d).
Median ratio actual / expected drop %1$s · ISF moved on %2$d of %3$d days, 20%% per day
%1$d meals: BG ended on average %2$s above where it started, so 1 U now covers fewer carbs.
%1$d meals: BG ended on average %2$s below where it started, so 1 U now covers more carbs.
%1$d meals: the carbs matched the insulin, IC stays.
%1$d meals, tuned day by day from the measured ratio.
No meals to look at, IC stays.
Carbs %1$s g ÷ insulin actually needed %2$s U = %3$s g/U · 20%% per day\nneeded = IOB before the meal + insulin given + insulin for the BG difference at the end
